useCases.title: Who it is for:| four situations, one approach
useCases.intro: A digital company produces rich documentation every day that is only ever used internally. It can be given value at several points in the life of the company.

items.title: Operating company
items.text: Documentation built up over years can generate revenue without giving up anything of your business: the licence is non-exclusive and you keep ownership of your content and your software.

items.title: Voluntary wind-down
items.text: In a dissolution or solvent liquidation, documentation becomes an asset with value, provided it is exported before online accounts are closed.

items.title: Divestment or product shutdown
items.text: When a business line is sold or a product discontinued, its documentation can be valued separately, in line with any commitments made elsewhere.

items.title: Judicial liquidation
items.text: With the liquidator and on authorization of the supervising judge: an asset usually worth nothing in the procedure becomes revenue for creditors.

scope.title: What we buy,| and what we do not
scope.intro: We acquire a non-exclusive licence of use on clearly defined written content. The scope is set out in writing before anything is signed.

buy.title: What we license
items: Wikis and Notion or Confluence spaces
Tickets: Jira, Linear, GitHub Issues
Specifications and design documents
Runbooks and postmortems
Code repository history, treated as data: commits, pull requests, reviews, links to tickets

notBuy.title: What we exclude
items: The software itself, the brand and the domain names
Messaging: Slack, Teams, email
Customer files and production databases
HR and legal spaces
Personal data of customers and employees
Code written for clients or under a third-party licence

scope.note: Ownership and exploitation of the software, brand and domain names remain entirely with the company, which stays free to sell them. We acquire no right to run, distribute or commercialize the software, nor to build a competing product.

process.title: How it works
process.intro: The steps depend on the company's situation. Choose your case.

steps.title: First conversation
steps.text: Initial contact and short qualification: tools used, type of content, specific constraints.

steps.title: Inventory under NDA
steps.text: Review of tools, volume and age of the content, under a non-disclosure agreement.

steps.title: Written proposal
steps.text: A proposal setting out the exact scope of the licensed content and the list of exclusions.

steps.title: Licence agreement
steps.text: Signature of a non-exclusive licence of use, limited to training and evaluating AI models.

steps.title: Export and anonymization
steps.text: Export of the content, anonymization, then deletion of the raw exports.

aside.title: What you get
items: Revenue from an asset that already exists
No transfer of ownership: your content and your software remain yours
Scope and exclusions agreed in writing
Export and anonymization carried out by us

steps.title: Case identification
steps.text: Identification of the company concerned and short qualification with the practitioner's office.

steps.title: Inventory under NDA
steps.text: Review of tools, volume and age of the content, under a non-disclosure agreement.

steps.title: Firm offer
steps.text: Offer in the usual French format: 10% deposit by bank cheque, bank certificate of funds, declaration of independence (art. L642-3 of the French Commercial Code), no conditions precedent.

steps.title: Authorization and deed
steps.text: Authorization by the supervising judge (juge-commissaire), then signature of the deed.

steps.title: Export and anonymization
steps.text: Export of the content, anonymization, then deletion of the raw exports.

aside.title: For the procedure
items: An asset usually worth nothing in the procedure becomes revenue
Export, anonymization and deed costs are borne by us
A protective export can be run before online accounts are closed for unpaid subscriptions
The software, brand and domain names stay in the estate and remain free to be sold

protection.title: Data protection
protection.intro: Confidentiality is a precondition of the business. Every export follows the same protocol.

items.title: Pseudonymized authors
items.text: Authors' names, usernames and addresses are replaced with pseudonyms.

items.title: Secrets removed
items.text: Keys, tokens and technical credentials are detected and removed.

items.title: Personal data removed
items.text: Customer names and personal data found in the text are removed.

items.title: Raw exports deleted
items.text: Original exports are deleted once the anonymized data has been delivered.

items.title: Limited, documented access
items.text: Only the people who need it can access exports, and every access is logged.

aiDevelopers.title: For AI developers
aiDevelopers.text: We build datasets drawn from real work: documentation, tickets, code reviews and the links between them. They are designed for training, evaluation and building reinforcement-learning environments.
items: Rights-cleared: every dataset rests on a written licence of use
Anonymized under a documented protocol
Traceable: the provenance of each dataset is tied to its licence

items.a: No. We only acquire a non-exclusive licence of use on the documentation. The software, brand and domain names remain the company's property, and it stays free to sell them. We acquire no right to run, distribute or commercialize the software.

items.q: Do you collect employees' messaging or emails?
items.a: No. Slack, Teams and email are excluded from the scope, as are HR and legal spaces, customer files and production databases.
Authors are pseudonymized, customer names and personal data found in the text are removed, and raw exports are deleted after delivery.

items.q: What is the content used for?
items.a: Only to train and evaluate artificial intelligence models. It is not used to build a competing product.
No. It is non-exclusive: the company keeps its content and can continue to use it as it wishes.

items.q: The online accounts are about to be closed. Is it too late?
items.a: Not necessarily. In a liquidation, we can run a protective export before accounts are closed for unpaid subscriptions. Contact us as early as possible.
